Email(s) 1: the automatic check did not match the copy to its assigned evidence. Review its claims against the sources; this check can miss paraphrases and does not establish whether a claim is true or invented.
What held the copy back: Some linked source pages could not be read; the corpus is partial: https://www.simpleanalytics.com/ - Use only the readable captured facts; do not infer missing prices, features or proof.
What would help most next time: Resolve this simulated next-step obstacle: I would have clicked if this email had told me that the linked review shows every outbound request and payload as well as the browser script and configuration. Check existing verified material first; surface a supported answer or documentation link appropriate to the CTA. If absent, obtain this specific information. Reader expectations are not product evidence.

Historical sources (2020-02-12); present applicability is not corroborated. Dutch municipalities have questions about what is and isn't permitted regarding cookies on their websites, and official guidance states that a public body cannot refuse website access to a citizen who does not give cookie consent, because citizens are dependent on their own municipa…
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. Official municipal guidance already names a specific privacy-friendly analytics alternative, and a local council has already formally asked the executive to actively pursue a privacy-friendly alternative to Google Analytics.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. Municipal cookie-consent banners vary widely: many sites run no banner, a self-built or unrecognized banner, or a professional consent-management platform such as CookieYes or Cookiebot.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. At least one municipality's website was found running Google Analytics tracking techniques together with Google's advertising network (DoubleClick).
Historical sources (2019-07-19); present applicability is not corroborated. Google Analytics was found to be the most-used third-party analytics tool on Dutch municipal websites, typically used because it is offered free of charge.
Historical sources (2020-02-12); present applicability is not corroborated. Official information-security guidance for municipalities describes removing the trailing octets of visitor IP addresses as a way to make an analytics cookie privacy-friendly.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. Being included in, and named by, a large-scale third-party scan of municipal websites' privacy practices that receives national media pickup.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. A city council member or political party submitting formal written questions (schriftelijke vragen) to the municipal executive about what tracking cookies the municipality's websites use and whether privacy-friendly alternatives will be sought.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. A city council asking the executive to actively seek a privacy-friendly alternative to Google Analytics.
Historical sources (2020-02-12); present applicability is not corroborated. Guidance for municipalities describes removing the trailing IP-address octets as a way to make an analytics cookie privacy-friendly enough that it does not require consent.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. The same study reports municipalities with no cookie banner at all, and separately, municipalities loading Google Analytics before consent, as co-occurring patterns across the municipal population.
Historical sources (2020-02-12); present applicability is not corroborated. Public bodies operate under an explicit, published legal position that access to a municipal website cannot be made conditional on cookie consent.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. Dutch security/tech news outlets cover the municipal scan findings, including public reader comments.
Historical sources (2020-02-12); present applicability is not corroborated. Official municipal information-security guidance (IBD) addresses cookie questions directly for gemeenten.
Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability. Formal council questions about municipal website tracking are published on a local political party's own site.
